news.title: Anthropic split Max into separate Max and Ultra plans
news.gist: Anthropic turned the Max 20x option into its own Ultra plan next to a flat $100 Max, and PricingSaaS argues that naming the top tier makes it a separate purchase that is easier to sell and justify than a toggle on a mid plan.
points: List prices stayed put: both plans sit at the two price points the old toggle offered, each with API credits matching its price
Ultra drops the 5-hour session limit for verified accounts, while Max lost its line promising higher output limits
The page doesn’t show whether weekly allowances changed, so heavy users should check which cap binds first before renewing
Max and Ultra appear only on the Individual tab, so Team and Enterprise buyers need to check their own pricing

news.why: If you pay for Max 20x, compare your heaviest week against Ultra’s weekly cap and Max’s 5-hour window before renewal, since the plan you land on now decides which limit stops you.

news.title: 10 Lessons on AI Credits from Gong, Miro, and Databricks
news.gist: Pricing leads from Gong, Miro and Databricks agree that AI credits work best as one pool tied to a familiar unit of work, with a cost per action the vendor can lower over time and spending controls ready on launch day.
points: Gong tested its AI role-play trainer on credits and pulled back, keeping lighter or immature features in the core plan
Miro is moving from charging for finished AI artifacts to charging for the agent work done, metered in stages
Databricks’ Mehra manages margin per workflow rather than per token, and passes model cost savings on to customers
The default allotment is monthly with no rollover; Mehra suggests partial rollover for enterprise deals
nums: credits per action in the example, a rate that can later drop to 0.3
changes the week’s roundup observed

3 months

news.why: When a vendor sells AI on credits, ask how many pools there are, what one credit buys in familiar terms and which per-user caps you can set, because those decide whether the bill can be forecast.

news.title: Anthropic splits Max into Max at $100 and Ultra at $200 a month in a 44-promo week
news.gist: PricingSaaS’s weekly review calls 26 Oct–1 Nov a busy week, well above its eight-week average, with promotions running at nearly twice their norm and contractions also far above usual.
points: Vercel quietly lowered firewall rule caps on every tier and added a metered deployment storage add-on
Baseten made previously hidden model prices public, and InVideo’s Max seat more than tripled as an annual discount ended
Shopify dropped its free Academy courses perk from all four plans without touching prices
Logz.io’s tracing cut was the week’s deepest, and Range’s Platinum plan was flagged as the biggest hike

news.title: Why the Labs are Giving away API Credits With Their Plans
news.gist: OpenAI and Anthropic handle heavy users of flat-rate plans by adding monthly API credits to top tiers instead of cutting limits, and Litterst argues SaaS vendors should copy them: keep the subscription and make extra usage easy to buy.
points: Cutting limits backfired: OpenAI reversed a cut to its top ChatGPT plan after pushback
The credits expire each billing cycle, don’t raise chat limits and skip entry plans such as Claude Pro and ChatGPT Plus
GitHub Copilot Pro+, HubSpot and Notion already include AI credits in their plans, so the idea is now flowing from labs to SaaS
The suggested first step is comparing cost to serve with revenue for the top tenth of users by AI usage

patterns.t: Heavy AI users get their own price points
patterns.p: AI vendors added room at the top: separate plans, higher price steps and bigger included allowances, while a cheap entry plan disappeared. Several of these come from PricingSaaS reports. Heavy users should check whether a new top tier beats paying for add-ons.

patterns.p: Per-minute and per-task AI prices fell at the application layer while GPU and AI infrastructure rates rose. Half of these come from PricingSaaS reports. Cheaper AI units today may be followed by smaller allowances if the cost underneath keeps climbing.

stats_analysis.t: Most changes make buyers pay more or get less
stats_analysis.p: Another 41 repackaged plans and 31 gave buyers more. The pay-more side is almost all smaller companies: 60 of the 64 sit in tier 3, and most of those records come from PricingSaaS reports rather than our own captures.

stats_analysis.t: The biggest changes mostly gave something back
stats_analysis.figNote: relevant changes that raised what buyers pay
stats_analysis.p: Of the 20 changes we flag as relevant, 8 gave buyers more and 8 repackaged plans. Datadog, Scribe and Aircall cut prices and GitHub and Figma folded features into existing seats; only Atlassian, Runpod, OVHcloud and Shopify went the other way, and the Atlassian and Shopify records come from PricingSaaS reports.

21 of the 23 increases are at tier-3 companies, mostly from PricingSaaS reports, and some are steep: InVideo’s Max seat and Katteb’s Lite plan more than doubled. Among tier-1 companies there was 1 increase (Atlassian Statuspage) and 1 cut (Datadog).

stats_analysis.t: Limits tightened more often than they loosened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that tightened vs loosened limits
stats_analysis.p: All 19 tightenings are at tier-3 companies, many of them free-plan caps such as Benchmark Email’s send limit and SE Ranking’s daily AI prompts. Loosenings reached bigger names: 2 of the 14 are relevant changes, at Wispr Flow and at Zoho Books, whose record comes from a PricingSaaS report.

stats_analysis.t: AI runs through a large share of the week
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that involve AI features, models or usage
stats_analysis.p: Among them, 4 moved AI between tiers, 2 put AI on a meter and 1 passed AI costs through. The direction is mixed: Perdoo and Nightwatch moved AI up to paid tiers while SugarCRM moved meeting prep down and Strawberry opened ChatGPT on every plan; all but SugarCRM come from PricingSaaS reports.

26 changes hit products sold to both businesses and consumers, and only 9 were consumer-only, such as Wispr Flow’s looser meeting limits. As in earlier weeks, our sources lean toward business pricing pages, so consumer moves are probably undercounted.

news_trends.t: AI subscriptions now come with API credits
news_trends.p: Anthropic and OpenAI answered heavy subscription use by bundling monthly API credits into upper tiers, and Anthropic’s Max split gives each price point its own matching allowance. The newsletter argues SaaS vendors are copying the move, and ClickUp’s pooled credits this week point the same way.

news_trends.t: Credit design is converging on one pool and simple units
news_trends.p: Since September the newsletter has moved from critiquing Notion’s two separate credit balances to a panel of pricing leads who all favour a single pool tied to a familiar unit. This week’s changes show vendors swapping odd allowances for credits or agent-usage tiers.
